title: Adaptive prefetch regulator and decode-fusion orchestrator to reduce tail latency
author: Lena Zhang
description: Context: On production workloads we observed sporadic token-level tail latency during bursts where prefill and decode contend for kernel slots and KV cache priming causes thrashing. This PR introduces two cooperating runtime components: 1) an Adaptive Prefetch Regulator (APR) that uses short-horizon workload sampling to budget KV priming by request class and to assign prefetch priority; 2) a Decode-Fusion Orchestrator (DFO) that dynamically chooses when to fuse prefill and decode microstages versus when to strictly separate them. Design: APR maintains per-route exponential moving averages for prefix hit-rate, sequence-length distribution, and recent kernel occupancy. It computes a per-request prefetch_budget and a priority token used by the scheduler. Budget is consumed during prefill; excess budget allows speculative KV warmups up to a configurable window. DFO uses a lightweight confidence signal (based on APR budget, queue length, and GPU kernel contention) to decide for each microbatch whether to route it through a fused prefill+decode kernel path (better overall throughput when confidence high) or keep the two-stage handoff (better tail latency when contention high). Implementation notes: APR is implemented in server/runtime/prefetch/regulator.cpp and exposed via a small control API to the scheduler. DFO logic lives in server/runtime/scheduler.cpp with new kernel flags in server/runtime/kernel_params.h. We added unit tests and microbenchmarks under tests/bench and test/runtime. Backwards compatibility: default configuration keeps behavior identical to main until operator flips feature_gate "adaptive_prefetch_fuse". Results: microbenchmarks (see tests/bench/prefetch_bench.py) show median throughput +7% and 99th percentile token latency -18% on a mixed conversational workload (batch sizes 8-32). On our Canary cluster the feature reduced burst tail spikes by 35% during a controlled load test. Rollout plan: feature-gated, start on Dedicated pools with canary traffic for 48h, then gradual ramp to 25% fleet, monitor token-99 and KV-miss-rate. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] benchmarks added [x] unit/integration tests [x] docs updated [x] feature-flagged [x] canary plan documented. Related: builds on measurements from ENG-4732 and complements kv prioritization work in ENG-5010.

release_notes: Adaptive Prefetch Regulator (APR) and Decode-Fusion Orchestrator (DFO) added behind feature gate 'adaptive_prefetch_fuse'. Enables dynamic prefetch budgeting and stage fusion decisions to reduce tail latency and improve throughput on bursty workloads. Default off; rollout plan documented in PR.
